title: What language does Linear A record, and can any proposed family beat chance?
short: Minoan Linear A can be roughly sounded out through Linear B values, but no proposed language family has been shown to fit better than random controls.

needs.ask: Write the Anatolian, Semitic and isolate hypotheses as explicit generative models and score them on held-out texts against shuffled sign values and unrelated control languages.
Build a single concordance of GORILA, its 2025 supplement, SigLA and lineara.xyz, encoding Linear B sound values in tiers from palaeographically secure to assumed.

matters: The language of Linear A bears on who the Minoans were, how Bronze Age Crete related to Anatolia, the Levant and Egypt, and what the Mycenaean Greeks inherited when they adapted the script as Linear B. Readings of personal names, toponyms and religious formulae on libation vessels would change accounts of Minoan religion and administration. A demonstration that no candidate family is detectable at this corpus size would also be a result, setting limits on what further comparative claims can mean.
stuck: The corpus is small and mostly administrative: about 1,430 documents in the original GORILA edition and 1,534 after the 2024–25 supplement, most of them short tallies, sealings and roundels, with roughly 7,500 signs in all. Linear B values give approximate pronunciations, but the transfer of values is itself an assumption, and many proposals (Luwian, Semitic, Hurrian, Tyrsenian and others) have been argued by selective lexical matching without controls for how many matches chance would produce. Few proposals have been stated in advance in a form that could fail.
solved: A language-family hypothesis, specified before testing (sound correspondences, morphology, lexicon), predicts readings of held-out inscriptions significantly better than the same procedure applied to shuffled sign values and unrelated control languages; or a power analysis shows that no such test can succeed at the current corpus size. A narrower solvable target is a complete, consistent account of the fraction signs and commodity totals (KU-RO) that balances the surviving tallies.
approach: The corpus is already well curated: Godart and Olivier (1976) and the supplement of Del Freo and Zurbach (2025) fix the texts, Salgarella and Castellan (2020) and lineara.xyz make them searchable, and Davis (2014) has edited the inscribed stone vessels that carry the libation formula. A first task is a single concordance across these, with transliteration uncertainty recorded sign by sign rather than resolved silently.

Which Linear B sound values to carry over is the decision that shapes every later test. Following Salgarella (2020), the corpus can be encoded in tiers, from values that are palaeographically secure to those that are merely assumed, so that each hypothesis is scored on the tier it depends on.

The accounting layer can be solved independently of the language. Extending Bennett (1950) and Corazza et al. (2021), fraction values and logogram totals can be treated as constraints that every complete tally ending in ku-ro must satisfy, as on HT 13, HT 85a and HT 94a; a balanced set of values would be useful even if no word is ever read.

The rival family hypotheses, Anatolian after Palmer (1958) and Finkelberg (1990), Semitic after Gordon (1966), and a non-Indo-European isolate favoured by Davis (2026), can each be written as an explicit generative model and pre-registered before scoring.

Each model is then scored against held-out texts using the cognate-alignment methods of Luo et al. (2019) and Luo et al. (2021), with the fictitious value assignments of Packard (1974) as a chance baseline. Scattered matches of the kind reported by Nepal and Perono Cacciafoco (2024) count only if they beat that baseline; the likeliest honest outcome is that every family is ranked, with intervals, rather than one confirmed.

Aegean epigraphers should review both the encoding and the scoring, ideally through the INSCRIBE project at Bologna, and permits to recheck doubtful signs on originals in the Heraklion Archaeological Museum would tighten the uncertain tier.

existing.title: Fractional Quantities in Minoan Bookkeeping
existing.note: First systematic attempt to assign values to the Linear A fraction signs from their use in tallies.

existing.title: Luvian and Linear A
existing.note: Proposed that the language of Linear A was Luwian or closely related Anatolian, the founding statement of the Anatolian hypothesis.

existing.title: Evidence for the Minoan Language
existing.note: Argued for a Northwest Semitic reading of Linear A; widely reviewed and not accepted by most Aegean specialists.

existing.title: Minoan Linear A
existing.note: Computer-assisted statistical study that compared Linear B sound values against fictitious reassignments, an early use of random controls for this script.

existing.title: Recueil des inscriptions en linéaire A (GORILA), vols. 1–5
existing.note: The standard corpus edition, with photographs, drawings and transliterations of roughly 1,430 inscriptions.

existing.title: Minoan Inscriptions on Libation Vessels
existing.note: Analyzed the religious 'libation formula' and argued that its morphology is compatible with an Anatolian language.

existing.title: Minoan Stone Vessels with Linear A Inscriptions
existing.note: Edition and study of the inscribed libation tables and ladles carrying the libation formula, arguing that Linear A records a non-Indo-European, non-Afroasiatic language, possibly verb-initial.

existing.authors: Jiaming Luo, Yuan Cao and Regina Barzilay
existing.title: Neural Decipherment via Minimum-Cost Flow: From Ugaritic to Linear B
existing.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the ACL: 3146–3155
existing.note: Unsupervised cognate-matching model that recovered known decipherments of Ugaritic and Linear B, a benchmark method for testing family hypotheses.

existing.title: Aegean Linear Script(s): Rethinking the Relationship between Linear A and Linear B
existing.note: Palaeographic and structural comparison of the two scripts, reassessing which Linear B values can safely be projected back onto Linear A.

existing.title: SigLA: The Signs of Linear A. A Palaeographical Database
existing.note: Searchable sign-by-sign database of Linear A documents with drawings, the main machine-readable resource for statistical work.

existing.authors: Michele Corazza, Silvia Ferrara, Barbara Montecchi, Fabio Tamburini and Miguel Valério
existing.title: The mathematical values of fraction signs in the Linear A script: A computational, statistical and typological approach
existing.note: Used exhaustive computation over candidate values, constrained by palaeography and typology, to propose a consistent set of fraction values for c. 1600–1450 BCE.

existing.authors: Jiaming Luo, Frederik Hartmann, Enrico Santus, Regina Barzilay and Yuan Cao
existing.title: Deciphering Undersegmented Ancient Scripts Using Phonetic Prior
existing.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 9: 69–81
existing.note: Extended the cognate model to unsegmented scripts with unknown relatives; identified known relatives for Gothic and Ugaritic and found no strong support for Basque as a relative of Iberian.

existing.authors: Aaradh Nepal and Francesco Perono Cacciafoco
existing.title: Minoan Cryptanalysis: Computational Approaches to Deciphering Linear A and Assessing Its Connections with Language Families from the Mediterranean and the Black Sea Areas
existing.note: Applied recent computational similarity methods to compare Linear A with Egyptian, Luwian, Hittite, Proto-Celtic and Uralic, reporting scattered matches and discussing the methods' limits.

existing.authors: Maurizio Del Freo and Julien Zurbach
existing.title: Recueil des inscriptions en linéaire A. Supplément 1 (RILA-S1)
existing.venue: Études crétoises 21.6. Athens: École française d'Athènes
existing.note: Adds 107 documents published through 2023, bringing the corpus to 1,534 documents and 7,574 signs; the CNR announcement dates it 2024.

existing.title: The Undeciphered Aegean Scripts: Linguistic Investigations into the Languages They Encode
existing.note: Applies 'syllabotactic' statistics to Linear A and the other undeciphered Aegean scripts and publishes the underlying data, building on his earlier argument for verb-initial word order.

archives.collection: Linear A tablets, roundels, nodules and inscribed stone vessels, including the Hagia Triada archive (HT series)
archives.note: Holds the majority of Linear A documents; study of originals requires a permit from the Greek Ministry of Culture, and some Hagia Triada material is in Rome and Florence.

holdings.name: Hagia Triada tablets (HT series)
holdings.note: Largest single group of Linear A tablets (147 in GORILA vol. 1), including the commodity tallies with ku-ro totals; originals are divided between Heraklion, Rome and Florence.

archives.repository: SigLA database (Cambridge / Rennes / University of Bologna INSCRIBE)
archives.collection: Sign-level palaeographic database of Linear A inscriptions
archives.note: Open access under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with hand drawings and sign, sequence and document search; coverage was still being extended after 2021.

holdings.name: HT 13
holdings.note: Hagia Triada tablet whose SigLA transcription ends in the total ku-ro, a test case for the commodity-sum analysis.

holdings.name: HT 85a
holdings.note: Hagia Triada tablet whose transcription ends in ku-ro, with transaction signs, for checking totals against entries.

holdings.name: HT 94a
holdings.note: Hagia Triada tablet with logograms and a ku-ro sequence, useful for the accounting-constraint work.

archives.collection: Interactive Linear A corpus with transliterations, findspot map and regular-expression search
archives.note: Open browsing and search over transliterated inscriptions, with sister sites for Linear B, Cretan Hieroglyphic and Cypro-Minoan; transliterations derive from GORILA and John Younger's former Kansas site.

archives.collection: Recueil des inscriptions en linéaire A (GORILA, Études crétoises 21.1–5) and Supplément 1 (Études crétoises 21.6)
archives.note: The authoritative print edition with photographs and facsimiles; not openly digitized, so a machine-readable concordance against it is a first task.

holdings.name: Recueil des inscriptions en linéaire A, Supplément 1 (RILA-S1)
holdings.note: Del Freo and Zurbach's supplement adding texts found since 1985 and published to 2023, bringing the corpus to 1,534 inscriptions.

holdings.name: Recueil des inscriptions en linéaire A (GORILA), vols. 1-5
holdings.note: Godart and Olivier's five-volume corpus (1976-1985) with photographs and drawings of each inscription.

archives.collection: Invention of Scripts and Their Beginnings (ERC project, PI Silvia Ferrara): Aegean script datasets and publications
archives.note: Hosts SigLA and the group behind the fraction-sign study of Corazza et al. (2021); a likely collaborator for held-out test design.
